content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: `AUDIT-EXPORT` backlog growth
Severity: SEV-2
Signal: audit-export backlog p95 > 25k for `sink=splunk` + elevated worker retries
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-export-overview
Primary: @Sean Gallagher

Sean Gallagher: seeing `splunk_hec_request{status=5xx}` spike since ~10:42. Backlog for a couple destinations climbing fast. Impact = delayed delivery to customer SIEM (beta). No primary API impact yet but worker CPU is pegged.

Allison Grant: confirming. Graphs:
- `audit_export_backlog_depth{sink="splunk"}` went 3k -> 38k in ~20m
- `audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds` p99 at 2,100s and rising
- worker retry rate is basically a retry storm

Rafael Mendes: pulling logs from `audit-export-worker` in prod.

Rafael Mendes: sample errors:
```
POST https://hec.customer.example/services/collector/event
status=503 body="Service Unavailable"
status=502 body="Bad Gateway"
status=504 body="Gateway Timeout"
request_id=ae_wkr_7f2c1 dest_id=dest_8Qh... tenant=tn_4c...
```
Looks like upstream HEC is intermittently failing. We keep retrying same batches.

Benji Okafor: queue semantics are at-least-once so retries are expected, but we probably need to trip circuit breaker earlier. Right now default backoff caps at 30s and max attempts is 0 (infinite) => we’ll hammer indefinitely.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Proposed immediate mitigation: pause the affected Splunk destinations to stop backlog growth + stop retry storm. Then we can coordinate w/ customer to fix HEC and replay.

Kevin Osei: pausing is OK from security standpoint; just make sure we leave a clear audit trail of config change + reason. Also: confirm we’re not dropping events (should buffer in queue).

Ethan Park: we can pause per destination via control plane. Benji can you run the pause for the two destinations showing worst backlog? I’ll double-check if any other tenants are impacted.

Allison Grant: top offenders by backlog:
- dest_8Qh… (tenant tn_4c…)
- dest_K1p… (tenant tn_9a…)
All other Splunk destinations look normal-ish (some minor 5xx but not exploding).

Benji Okafor: ack. pausing those now.

Benji Okafor: ran:
```
ri-admin audit-export destination pause --dest dest_8Qh... --reason "HEC 5xx retry storm (SEV-2 incident)"
ri-admin audit-export destination pause --dest dest_K1p... --reason "HEC 5xx retry storm (SEV-2 incident)"
```
Both returned `state=paused`.

incident-bot: :information_source: Status update: Destination state changes detected
- dest_8Qh… => paused
- dest_K1p… => paused

Rafael Mendes: retry rate dropping already. Worker CPU starting to normalize.

Aisha Bello: backlog depth stopped climbing on those two (flatlining). Global `splunk` backlog still elevated but no longer increasing.

Sean Gallagher: cool. Next: tune retry/backoff to prevent future storms even when not paused. Benji/Ethan, can we hotpatch config to increase backoff + add 5xx circuit breaker? Even a quick cap like “pause after N consecutive 5xx” would help.

Benji Okafor: we can’t ship new logic instantly, but we *can* adjust runtime config for splunk connector:
- lower batch size (currently 500 events / request)
- raise backoff max (30s -> 5m)
- add jitter (already on)
I can push config change in the worker config map.

Rafael Mendes: +1 lowering batch size may reduce timeouts on their HEC if it’s choking on payload size.

Marcus Lin: make sure lowering batch size doesn’t increase overall request rate too much during recovery. If they’re rate limiting + intermittently 5xx, more requests could worsen.

Allison Grant: right now we’re in “paused” state for the two destinations, so it’s safe to change defaults before resuming. For the rest, request rate is stable.

Connor O'Brien: can take point on safe rollout (canary one worker pool). If we change config map, it’ll restart pods. That’s OK but let’s do it gradually.

Sean Gallagher: plan:
1) update splunk connector config: backoff cap 5m, batch size 200
2) restart worker pool in canary (10%)
3) watch metrics: request rate, 5xx, backlog

Benji Okafor: I’ll prep the config diff.

Benji Okafor: proposed changes:
```
SPLUNK_BATCH_MAX_EVENTS=200   # was 500
SPLUNK_RETRY_BACKOFF_MAX=300s # was 30s
SPLUNK_RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE=2s  # unchanged
SPLUNK_RETRY_JITTER=true      # unchanged
```
This is global for splunk connector.

Rafael Mendes: 300s (5m) seems good. we should also cap max in-flight retries per destination but that’s code.

Ethan Park: agreed. for now, this reduces hammering and buys time.

Connor O'Brien: ok to roll. I’ll do canary restart of worker deployment.

Connor O'Brien: rolled 10% canary (`audit-export-worker` 2/20 pods restarted). Watching.

Allison Grant: seeing canary pods pick up work w/ new config; request rate down slightly. No abnormal errors.

Rafael Mendes: since the two big destinations are paused, we won’t test 5xx behavior until resumed. But this should prevent storm once we re-enable.

Sean Gallagher: comms: we should loop Solutions Eng to notify affected beta customers. I’ll ping @Colin O'Donnell / @Fatima Noor offline with dest IDs + impact.

Kevin Osei: also please ensure we capture in the incident notes that data remained buffered and that resuming may cause duplicates due to at-least-once semantics. Customer should dedupe on event_id.

Sean Gallagher: yup.

incident-bot: :memo: Incident notes updated by Sean Gallagher
- Cause: customer Splunk HEC intermittently returning 5xx -> connector retry storm -> backlog growth
- Mitigation: paused affected destinations (dest_8Qh…, dest_K1p…), tuned retry backoff + reduced batch size, canary rollout

Aisha Bello: metrics now:
- worker CPU back to baseline
- `audit_export_dlq_writes_total` unchanged (no DLQ growth)
- overall backlog slowly decreasing as other destinations drain

Rafael Mendes: confirm no drop. queue depth stable, no evidence of message loss.

Sean Gallagher: next step once customer confirms HEC stable: unpause one destination and monitor. not doing that during incident.

Ethan Park: agreed. also we should add an alert for “consecutive 5xx per destination” + auto-degrade state, but that’s for follow-up.

Allison Grant: I’ll add a quick panel to dashboard for per-dest 5xx + retry rate (if labels exist). Right now it’s aggregated.

Sean Gallagher: OK. marking incident mitigated (service stable, backlog growth stopped). Keep open until we confirm resume plan w/ customers.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status changed: Investigating -> Monitoring
Owner: Sean Gallagher

Sean Gallagher: monitoring for 30m. If no further backlog growth, we can close and track follow-ups in ENG tickets (circuit breaker, per-dest retry limits, better error classification).

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: will keep an eye on `splunk_hec_request{status=5xx}`.

Connor O'Brien: canary looks fine; ready to roll the rest of worker pods if we decide.

Sean Gallagher: go ahead and roll remaining pods now since change is low risk and reduces blast radius.

Connor O'Brien: rolled remaining 90% (rolling restart complete).

Allison Grant: all green post-roll. no spike in error rate.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved criteria met (backlog growth stopped, worker stable). Please add follow-ups before closing.

Sean Gallagher: adding follow-ups in separate thread + Linear. Closing this incident thread once notes are finalized.
